import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_89/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_89/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Perform the JOIN on 'city' between Source2_89_0 and Source2_89_1
# According to operation history, join keys are ['city', 'city']
# But the intermediate_step1.csv after join only has ['city', 'fare'], so the join is effectively to keep Source0 rows with matching city in Source1
# We do an inner join to keep only cities present in both sources
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1[['city']], on='city', how='inner')

# Group by city and sum the fare from Source2_89_0 (joined DataFrame)
grouped = joined.groupby('city', as_index=False)['fare'].sum()

# Ensure the schema matches target: ['city': string, 'fare': float]
grouped['city'] = grouped['city'].astype(str)
grouped['fare'] = grouped['fare'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target path
grouped.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_89/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_89/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (inner join to keep only matching cities)
